price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: offensive reorganization (displacement D_real of the play-type mix)
regression to the mean and mechanical coupling of play-type mix and PPP
methodological_questions: Does reorganization beyond what L_pre predicts correlate with the during-spell minus pre-spell change in team PPP?
Is D_real reliable enough per spell, with sparse possessions, to separate signal from its noise floor?
Is the play-type mix shift mechanically coupled to PPP, because play types differ in league-wide efficiency?
Do absent-player quality, opponent, schedule and injury selection confound the relationship?
With 148 spells, what minimum detectable correlation is available and is it adequate?

historical_evidence.finding: Real absences moved the association structure: V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, V1(b) mean(D_real - median null) +0.142 CI [+0.103,+0.187]. The magnitude prediction from the LOO simulation failed: V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244,+0.667]; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115. The record lists the limitation LIM:small_sample.

Team offensive association structure persists across split halves (Frobenius P1a S=0.352, p<0.01) and is not reducible to play-type rates (residual R2=0.043). This supports the structural measure as a stable team property.

Connector absence displaced offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched role-occupant absence: paired dD_A +0.1151, n=96 matched pairs, p=7e-09. Terminal-scorer comparison n=25, p=0.026. The record flags RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, and the licensed comparison excludes organizers.

Pre-game play-type PPP rankings correlated with actual rankings in held-out games (median rho +0.539, 908 game-team rows). The record's failure mechanism is C_artifact: part of the top-3 lift reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION). It also lists RISK:DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY.

Replacement-player similarity did not separate absorb from cascade after an absence (Spearman(sim,-gap) = -0.19, wrong-signed). It is recorded as a powered null with label-classification error as a limitation.
The model-scored routing gain shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on the larger 520-matchup sample. The record notes the results are model-scored, not observed outcomes.
Apparent play-type lag effects on PPP (n>150k) were flat and collapsed under a within-team baseline. The record names a team-quality confound (RISK:CONFOUNDING).
DRIVE and PNR lag-1 PPP effects disappeared with game-state controls and a within-team baseline; only SPOT_UP lag-1 survived.
Global lag lifts disappeared after team-season demeaning.
A single-game validation (BOS vs OKC) was inconclusive: one game, 4-35 possessions per play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of real absence reorganization from the leave-one-out simulation (V2a/V2b), n=23
failed_approaches.why: Spearman +0.29 and +0.25 with CIs spanning zero (about -0.25 to +0.67). Recorded outcome status 'untestable', with LIM:small_sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive pooled play-type to PPP associations (lag effects)
failed_approaches.why: The apparent effect was produced by team-quality confounding and vanished under within-team baselines (artifact; RISK:CONFOUNDING).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive play-type to PPP effects without game-state controls
failed_approaches.why: The effects disappeared once period, clock, margin and within-team baselines were controlled (artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooled play-type to PPP effects without team-season demeaning
failed_approaches.why: The effect was a between-team artifact (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Model-scored value gains from play-type routing
failed_approaches.why: The gain shrank to near zero on the larger sample (powered null, B_powered_null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Similarity of the replacement player as a predictor of absorb vs cascade
failed_approaches.why: Wrong-signed null; label error (LABEL_ERROR) is recorded as a limitation.

evidence_establishes: Per the records, the project's structural displacement measure responds to real absences above its null (FAM:SF20 V1) and is a persistent team property (FAM:SF17).
Per the records, displacement differs by absent-player role at n=96 matched pairs (FAM:SF-APPS-088).
Per the records, pooled play-type to PPP associations are repeatedly vulnerable to team-quality and game-state confounding (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-037, FAM:SF-APPS-073).
Per the records, the one attempt to predict the magnitude of displacement from simulated L-based structure was inconclusive at n=23 (FAM:SF20).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether reorganization magnitude, with or without scaling by L, predicts the change in PPP. No retrieved record tests reorganization against PPP change in absence spells.
The direction of any relationship, since reorganization might signal adaptation or breakdown.
Whether the 148-spell sample is enough, since the one related prediction test (n=23) had a CI too wide to say anything.
The reliability of per-spell D_real, or the size of its noise floor, at the possession counts of 148 spells.
own_inferences: Reading 'relative to L' as reorganization compared with the amount expected from L_pre is my interpretation, based on the glossary definition of L. It is not stated in the task.
The ratio D_real/L_pre has a noisy denominator, so it is less safe than the residual of D_real on L_pre. I prefer the residual.
Large reorganization probably marks the absence of a more important player, who also lowers PPP. Without controls the correlation would mostly show absent-player quality.
Because play types differ in league-wide efficiency, any mix shift mechanically moves expected PPP. I would credit only the part of a PPP change not explained by the play-type mix shift.

At n=148 the minimum detectable rho is about 0.23 (80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05, independent spells). Clustering of spells within team-seasons would raise it. A true rho below about 0.2 cannot be ruled out and would likely end as inconclusive.
The artifact outcome is a substantial probability given the project's history of pooled PPP effects vanishing under within-team baselines.
uncertainties: The exact definitions of 'reorganization' and 'L' (L_pre) in the task.
The meaning of 'n=986' versus '148 spells', and the minimum spell length (the main studies used at least 15 games).
How many of the 148 spells overlap within a team-season or share a roster.
Whether D_real noise floors and null medians are available per spell.
Whether the 2025-26 partial data are complete enough to be included.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the records I might have proceeded plainly. FAM:SF20 shows that the nearest magnitude-prediction test (n=23) was inconclusive. The artifact records (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-037, FAM:SF-APPS-073) show that pooled PPP effects tend to be confounding artifacts. That moved the decision to proceed_with_changes: a within-team baseline, a pre-registered null-floor-corrected measure and a defined minimum informative effect. The records do not answer the question itself.

blocking_constraints.text: With 148 spells the minimum detectable |rho| is about 0.23 before clustering and control adjustment. Smaller true effects are not detectable, and the n=23 predecessor (FAM:SF20) was inconclusive.
Per-spell D_real depends on sparse possessions and has a noise floor. Without a null-corrected measure, reliability attenuates any correlation.
Absent-player quality, usage and team strength drive both reorganization and the PPP change. Pooled estimates are not interpretable without controls (FAM:SF-CHT-029).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether reorganization magnitude predicts the change in PPP during absence spells. The nearest, FAM:SF20, tested predicting displacement magnitude at n=23 and was inconclusive. Several related records show that pooled play-type to PPP effects fail under within-team controls. The question is therefore not answered, and it is informed mainly by cautionary precedent.

risks.text: 148 spells give an MDE of about rho 0.23 and little power for realistic small effects. Spells nested in team-seasons reduce the effective n.
D_real and L_pre are estimated from limited possessions. Noise inflates D_real and can create a spurious relationship with the PPP change. The ratio to L_pre is unstable when L_pre is small.
D_real has a positive floor under pure noise (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF20 null). It must be compared with a per-spell null rather than with zero.

The play-type mix and PPP both come from the same possessions. A mix shift toward efficient play types (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION) moves PPP by construction (FAM:SF-APPA-063). Control for mix-implied PPP.
Spells follow injuries, and baseline windows may be unusually high or low in PPP. The PPP change then regresses toward the mean independently of reorganization.

Absent-player quality, replacement quality, schedule, opponent strength, other absences, trades and in-season coaching changes. Pooled effects in FAM:SF-CHT-029 and FAM:SF-CHT-037 vanished under controls.
There are many possible definitions of reorganization (cosine, Frobenius, ratio, residual) and PPP change. All must be pre-specified.
Seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 may differ in league play-type efficiency. Standardize within season.
Play-type classifier errors add noise to the mix and to D_real (FAM:SF-CHT-052).

design.estimand: Partial Spearman correlation between excess reorganization and the PPP change per spell. Excess reorganization = D_real minus the value expected from L_pre and the per-spell null floor. PPP change = during-spell minus pre-spell team PPP (garbage time excluded), net of the PPP implied by the shift in play-type mix. Two-sided; direction not assumed.
design.unit: Absence spell (player missing at least 15 consecutive games, as in the main studies; the 148 listed spells), with team-season as the cluster.
design.sample: All 148 spells from NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs, 2025-26 only when complete). Fix the inclusion rules, minimum possessions per window and treatment of overlapping spells before looking at outcomes. Prefer the first spell per team-season if overlap is heavy. Report the effective n.
design.power: At n=148 independent spells and alpha 0.05, an MDE of |rho| of about 0.23 at 80% power. Reduce for clustering and control adjustment (expect about 0.25-0.28). Pre-specify the smallest effect of interest at |rho| = 0.25 and treat a CI excluding it as an equivalence result. Do not claim a null if the CI is wider than the pre-specified interval.
design.controls: Within-team baseline using the pre-spell window of the same team-season. Control for the absent player's usage, minutes and on/off or L_pre, pre-spell PPP (for RTM), opponent strength and rest, replacement quality, and share of the spell in playoffs. Standardize within season. Use a possession-count weight or noise-floor correction in D_real. Compute the mix-implied PPP from season-standardized play-type PPP and verify that results hold with and without it.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: a pseudo-spell at random pre-absence windows for the same teams should give rho near 0. (2) Permute D_real across spells within season, and also compare against the per-spell null floor. (3) A negative control: a team's PPP change in the next season-window with the same L_pre. (4) Verify that a split-half D_real correlates positively across halves; if split-half reliability is below about 0.3, report as untestable.
design.multiplicity: One primary test: the residual-based excess reorganization in cosine distance vs the mix-adjusted PPP change. Secondary: Frobenius distance, the ratio D_real/L_pre, and unadjusted PPP change. These are reported with Holm correction and labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary partial rho has |rho| at least 0.25 with the cluster-bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0, a consistent sign across at least three of four seasons, and survival in the placebo and mix-adjusted checks. Rejected if the CI lies within [-0.25, 0.25]. Artifact if the raw association disappears after controls or mix adjustment. Otherwise inconclusive.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-11-01. Freeze the extract with a hash, classifier version and the spell list, and pre-register before any outcome analysis.

methodological_questions: Does the magnitude of offensive reorganization predict the change in points per possession?
How is reorganization measured relative to baseline L and is the measure reliable with sparse possessions per spell?
Is the reorganization measure mechanically tied to the PPP outcome or confounded by absent player quality, opponent, and regression to the mean?
Is the sample of absence spells sufficient to detect a correlation (n=148 spells, minimum detectable rho)?
args.query: player absence spells: does the degree of offensive reorganization relative to baseline L predict change in points per possession; prior studies on absence, play-type shift, reliability, regression to the mean, and power

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs

Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

TOOL_RESULT glossary:
# Terminology used in the research questions

This glossary is given identically in every condition. It defines terms only and reports no results. Definitions follow the published papers (Structural Influence; Detecting Defensive Suppression) where they exist.

- **Possession, PPP:** a team's continuous spell with the ball; PPP is points per possession.
- **H1, H2:** first half (periods 1 and 2) and second half (periods 3 and 4) of a game. RS and PO: regular season and playoffs.
- **Play type:** the label assigned to each possession by the project's rule-based classifier from play-by-play events. Labels include PNR (pick-and-roll ball handler), DRIVE, CUT, SPOT_UP, PULL_UP, POST_UP, PUTBACK and TRANSITION. A play-type mix is a team's share of possessions in each play type.
- **Initiator, initiation:** the offensive player whose action starts the possession's play type (for example the cutter on a cut, the ball handler on a pick-and-roll). Initiation records are possession-level rows linking initiator, play type and points.
- **Inferrer:** the classifier step that infers a play type (for example a pick-and-roll) from play-by-play text when it is not recorded directly.
- **Suppression trigger:** a team, play type and game in which the team's PPP on that play type falls sharply from H1 to H2 under fixed minimum-attempt rules; read as the defense possibly taking the action away.
- **Continuation, counter:** after a trigger, continuation means the offense keeps running the triggered play type; a counter is a different play type run instead.
- **BEST, AVOID (counter tiers):** the strategy app's matchup-ranked counter recommendations after a trigger. BEST is the top-ranked counter play type for that matchup, AVOID the lowest-ranked.
- **Structural fingerprint:** a team's standardized pattern of how play types share initiators.
- **Structural influence (load, L):** how much a team's structural fingerprint changes when one player's initiations are removed. L_pre is that quantity measured from games before an absence.
- **Usage:** a player's share of team possessions he initiates or finishes.
- **Role categories (Structural Influence paper):** by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (structural influence beyond what usage predicts): Primary Organizer (high usage, positive residual), Shaper (low usage, positive residual), Terminal Scorer (high usage, residual at or below zero), Role Occupant or Specialist (low usage, residual at or below zero).
- **Connector:** a structural-role label used in later studies for players whose presence links teammates' play types; the exact rule varied between studies.
- **Hub:** a high-structural-influence player around whom a team's initiations are organized.
- **Absence spell:** a run of consecutive games a player misses (the main studies used at least 15).
- **Displacement (D_real):** how far teammates' play-type mix moves during an absence spell relative to before it (one minus the cosine similarity of the two mixes).
- **Mover, decoy:** a mover is a player who changed teams between seasons; decoys are comparison players used as placebo matches for a mover.
- **Stint:** an interval of play with the same ten players on the court.
- **Garbage time:** late-game possessions with a lopsided score, usually excluded.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm treating L as the structural load before the absence, and checking how much the offense reorganizes relative to that baseline, using the leave-one-out simulation prediction. The earlier SF20 V2 comparison of simulated magnitude against real displacement failed, with rho 0.288 at n=23. Here the outcome is the change in PPP across 148 spells, and I'm thinking about the minimum detectable rho. I'm leaning toward wrapping this up, though I'm still weighing whether to pull up the SF20 family details first.

I'm settling the design around a partial correlation between the reorganization ratio and the change in team PPP, controlling for the absent player's pre-absence usage and the opponent. With 148 spells the minimum detectable rho comes out near 0.23, but I need to watch for mechanical coupling: the ratio is built from the same fingerprint change, and play-type mix shifts can move PPP on their own. Absent-player quality could also drive both measures at once, and spells chosen for absence invite regression to the mean.

I'm checking the noise floor in the reorganization measure, since sparse possessions could inflate it, and the SF20 null medians give a baseline. I'll require at least 15 games per spell and use a noise-floor-corrected displacement. The sign of the prediction isn't specified, so I'm planning a two-sided test, with a partial correlation controlling for the absent player's usage, pre-absence load, and minutes share. The real question seems to be whether reorganization beyond what L predicts relates to the PPP change.

I'm noting that the SF-APPA-017 result is rejected and SF-APPA-035 can't be tested, and that none of the records tests PPP change against reorganization directly. I'll also say clearly that the reading of L comes from the glossary.
